dense_vs_specialized.source: same process/population/rows: specialized = prefix part anchor, dense = EVOGP_EVAL_MODE=dense part

const.note: constant tree: nothing to compile and nothing to run, so the warm time is the pure per-call overhead

decomposition.note: single_tree_call_ms = per_call_overhead + per_tree_run (both measured with the SAME executable); the single-tree call is what _sample_model times once per tree, while a full population pays per_call_overhead once

dense.note: EVOGP_EVAL_MODE=dense on the same forest/inputs as the prefix part (ONE graph for the whole population)

dense_vs_specialized.source: same process/population/rows: specialized = prefix part anchor, dense = EVOGP_EVAL_MODE=dense part

identical.note: a forest of anchor_pop copies of tree 0 (single program, cache hit unless the prefix part did not run first)

sample.note: the exact _sample_model loop: clear_cache() + gc.collect() before every tree; effective_ms divides the per-tree time by the anchor pop, i.e. what the old model extrapolates

single_hit.note: single-tree Forest, cache NOT cleared: every call is a hit, so this isolates the single-tree call overhead from the rebuild
